statement: On gsi sha256 9eca674b79248987e67d458c9acce7941149f428616caf0aff5defdc93e49d78, one thread-interrupt! flood of 100000 iterations times 10 threads at -:p11 finished in about 2s on the fast schedule and did not finish within 8s or 20s on the other schedule. Eight later trials were 3 passes and 5 stops. The same flood with -:m64M finished 16 of 16 times inside 8s. One 1000000-iteration flood at -:p11,m64M finished in about 10.5s and the next one was still inside select after 16s. A one-second sample of that stop shows the idle path ___device_select(NULL, 0, 0, 0, timeout) inside __select for about 735 of 748 hits, with the same threads also entering barrier_sync_op and mark_reachable_from_marked. A 10ms device-less select bound, a guard against re-raising a stale current-thread interrupt, and a 64MB default floor compiled into a scratch gsi did not make 8 of 8 runs finish. Routing every Scheme btq and mutex lock through ##lock-scheduler-object-with-sync-participation! scored 5 of 8, and one stop died in cleanup with retained runtime resources. None of these runs is a GC/FFI inventory PASS. The count stays 8/12.
rejectedRepair: 10ms idle select bound; stale current-thread re-raise guard; 64MB minimum-heap floor; idle-select flag plus a level-triggered abort byte (1 of 8); Scheme btq/mutex sync-participation trylock (5 of 8); ##sync-op-interrupt! before idle ##wait! plus a select skip (0 of 4); forced abort whenever the self-pipe exists (1 of 4); a bogus absolute 0.02s idle timeout that returned immediately (0 of 6 and 0 of 8); a real now+20ms idle deadline (4 of 8 at 100000, 2 of 6 at 1000000); skipping idle select when the high-level interrupt queue or any flag is pending (3 of 8 at 100000, 1 of 6 at 1000000); writing every self-pipe at barrier entry and refusing device-less select while ___sync_barrier_open is set (the first 100000 trial wedged at startup for over 5 minutes and did not answer SIGTERM); an extra nonblocking self-pipe write from ___raise_high_level_interrupt_pstate when writing_fd > 2 (1000 iterations finished, two 100000 -:p11 floods killed at 20s with no output). Those edits were not kept.
wakeProbe: On a wedged origin gsi, select nfds/fd pairs were (7,6), (9,8), (11,10), (13,12). write() of one byte to fd 7 returned 1. The matching processor then entered service_sync_op for a few samples and went back to select. The other processors stayed in select. ___cleanup then fails resize-to-1, sets cleanup_phase to retained, and prints cleanup failed with retained runtime resources.

maskedOther.mechanism: ___raise_high_level_interrupt_pstate queues the interrupt and calls ___raise_interrupt_pstate with ___INTR_OTHER. ___disable_interrupts_pstate leaves only ___INTR_SYNC_OP enabled, which is the state inside ##wait!. ___INTERRUPT_REQ is then false, so the self-pipe is not written. device_select still watches that pipe.
maskedOther.result: The extra nonblocking self-pipe write was compiled into ____raise_high_level_interrupt_pstate. A 1000-iteration flood finished PROBE-DONE 10000. Two 100000-iteration -:p11 floods produced no output and were killed at 20s. The edit was removed. This does not close GC/FFI.
maskedOther.originTiming: On the restored origin gsi, -:p11 finished 1000 in 0.05s, 10000 in 0.22s, 20000 in 0.44s, 40000 in 0.89s and again in 0.97s, 45000 in 1.02s, and 55000 in 1.19s. 50000, 60000, 80000, and 100000 produced no output; 100000 was killed at 90s. A one-second sample during a 100000 run showed all 11 processors cycling through __select, barrier_sync_op condvar waits, and mark_reachable_from_marked waits, with one processor also in ___H___eval. A later sample, 12s into the hang, still had nine processors mostly in select and one in ___call. The hang is intermittent and more likely as the iteration count grows. It is not a hard capacity cliff.
maskedOther.whySelectReturns: ___device_select drains every byte from the abort pipe, then the idle path can ##wait! again. The first 48 device-less blocks in a 100000 -:p11 run had scheduler_status 1 (processor 0 sometimes 0), ___INTR_SYNC_OP 0, ___INTR_OTHER 0, and an empty processor high-level queue. After the byte is drained there is no interrupt state left for select to observe. A one-shot latch after a drained abort byte finished 3 of 8. A masked pipe write plus ##other-interrupt! before idle ##wait! finished 1 of 8. Acknowledging ___INTR_SYNC_OP so a newer raise survives the clear finished 5 of 8, and adding the masked write finished 3 of 8. That acknowledge left the flag clear even when the sequence moved, so it did not re-arm the wake. Publishing in-select and writing for masked ___INTR_OTHER only then, while also not blocking when that flag was already set, finished 2 of 8; the variant that also polled on ___INTR_SYNC_OP finished 1 of 8. A per-collective epoch join from select finished 6 of 8 and then 3 of 8. Queuing the high-level interrupt under the processor lock and then calling ##wait-abort-no-remove! finished 0 of 8. Draining the processor queue before idle ##wait! finished 2 of 8. Pinning the target to processor 0 on the origin gsi finished 6 of 8 in about 1.8s. Placing a not-current target on its last processor and calling ##wait-abort-no-remove! finished 7 of 8 in one batch and 4 of 8 in a later batch. Writing one abort byte only when that pipe was empty, on the not-current path, finished 3 of 8 and was removed. Adding the same wake on the current-thread path finished 0 of 8 and was removed. Re-arming the flag and the abort pipe when a newer ___INTR_SYNC_OP raise lands during the clear, and staying in the barrier while that flag is set, finished 1 of 8. The same re-arm without the extra barrier round finished 4 of 8. Both were removed. ___sync_wait is still only ___CONDVAR_WAIT. Draining the current thread's interrupt queue on the ##thread-yield! fast path, and skipping ##btq-insert! when the target had become current, finished 4 of 8 and was removed. Publishing in-select and returning before select when ___INTR_OTHER was already set, while writing the pipe for a masked ___INTR_OTHER only inside select, finished 3 of 8. The same pipe write without that early return finished 4 of 8. Both were removed. ___sync_wait did not re-raise ___INTR_SYNC_OP. A heartbeat probe on that wake showed workers stop inside thread-interrupt! after partial progress: one run finished, two froze after beats 880000 and 900000, and one froze after beat 120008. ##other-interrupt! now drains the running thread's interrupt queue, and a not-current send that finds the target already current does not also ##btq-insert! it. Two 100000 -:p11 batches of that edit finished 6 of 8 and 6 of 8. The same binary at -:p2 finished 2 of 4. A p2 sample at beat 940000 still had one processor in ___H___eval and ___H___num and the other in __select. Calling ##other-interrupt! from the yield fast path finished 4 of 4 at -:p2 and 4 of 8 at -:p11, and was removed. Draining only the thread queue from that fast path finished 0 of 4 at -:p2 and 4 of 8 at -:p11, and was removed. Calling ##other-interrupt! and then ##thread-yield! again when that left a runnable thread finished 1 of 4 at -:p2 and 3 of 8 at -:p11, and was removed. Skipping device-less select when ___INTR_SYNC_OP was already set finished 5 of 8 and was removed. The p11 flood was not submitted to gambit-smp because no 100000 batch was 8 of 8. A one-second sample of a hung run showed ten processors mostly in __select and barrier_sync_op, and one processor in ___H___eval and ___H___num. The collective is entered and left. The mutator keeps running while the other processors sit idle. The last-processor placement remains in the 4463 _thread.scm. It is not 8 of 8. The untouched origin gsi finished 4 of 8. Origin gsi sha256 is unchanged.

runningProcessorScan.secondLockStall: A counter build of that 7 of 8 source, later removed, showed a frozen hang with propagate enter equal to leave, terminated drops 0, and the second mutex-lock enter exactly one ahead of its leave. The high-level run count and the resume run count stopped while the target kept taking the empty-queue yield path. One result mutex stays owned and its thunk is not run. An in-flight list that redelivered a request after eight rescue scans scored 2 of 8 and was removed. The binary was rebuilt from the 7 of 8 source. Linking the same interrupt on the thread queue through slot 0 and on the processor queue through slot 2, and running the thunk only after a compare-and-swap, crashed with EXC_BAD_ACCESS at address 0x57 in ___H___thread. Replacing the second mutex-lock with an owner poll that yields, and yielding after the handler unlock, each hung a 1000-iteration flood with no output. Those edits were removed. Clearing a null head's tail scored 3 of 8. Restoring the head from that tail scored 4 of 8. Both were removed. A restored 1000-iteration smoke printed PROBE-DONE 10000 in 0.540s. os_join_error_then_success returns false when the transcript is not exactly an OS join errno then same-owner 0, and the banner returns false before that match. Origin gsi sha256 is unchanged. The count stays 8/12. Skipping a processor-queue self-loop scored 3 of 8 and was removed. Linking the running target only onto its thread queue while the thread lock was held, then raising ___INTR_OTHER without ##raise-high-level-interrupt, scored 5 of 8 (passes at 1.985s, 9.453s, 7.013s, 2.975s, 4.007s; three kills at 12s) and was removed. The restored 1000-iteration smoke printed PROBE-DONE 10000 in 0.535s. Origin gsi sha256 is unchanged. Count stays 8/12.
runningProcessorScan.statement: Clue continuation clue-read:28b7184a58b4d6af4803eddce62c454bb8cee70a9f3828574ce926df9d6f1c57. The registered processor-interrupt view stays unclosed on child-progress-correspondence and collective-interpreted-qualification, executionAuthorized false, runtimeAdmitted false. An unlocked scan that raises ___INTR_OTHER on the processor actually running the target finished 7 of 8 at 100000 -:p11. Forcing stack_trip on that raise finished 3 of 8 and was removed. When the yield fast path sees a non-empty thread interrupt queue it now takes the existing save/schedule path, whose resume drains that queue. Two 100000 -:p11 batches of that edit finished 7 of 8 and 7 of 8, and -:p2 finished 3 of 4. A sample still had ten processors in __select and one in ___H___eval and ___H___num. Putting the already-current send on the thread queue instead of ##raise-high-level-interrupt finished one 8 of 8 batch and then 4 of 8, and was removed. Calling ##other-interrupt! from the yield fast path only when the processor high-level queue was non-empty finished 4 of 8 at -:p11 and 2 of 4 at -:p2, and was removed. Publishing a masked interrupt flag with a barrier and no stack trip finished 6 of 8 and was removed. A who-probe showed a hang where worker beats stopped at 196 of 200 while the target kept yielding, so the thread queue was empty and the remaining interrupts were not on that thread. Waking idle processors whose high-level queue was non-empty, and draining that queue after select returned, finished 3 of 8 and was removed. Draining that queue from the idle processor after select, with no extra wake, also finished 3 of 8 and was removed. Running only the current thread's own high-level thunks from the yield fast path finished 2 of 8 and was removed. Moving the already-current send onto the thread queue and running those thunks from the yield fast path finished 1 of 4 at -:p2 and 6 of 8 at -:p11, and was removed. A yield-fast-path scan during one hang saw the target yield 1120000 times while every processor high-level queue stayed empty, so the stuck interrupt is not waiting on those queues. The scan was removed. Line 502 returns false unless the stdout is exactly OS-JOIN-ERROR then SAME-OWNER-JOIN 0, and the banner returns false before that match. The recovery-1 setup.c still stores ___LW_REFUSED before ___thread_join, then joins only after handler_quiet and gets ___NO_ERR. ___thread_join is pthread_join. That is not a still-joinable OS error followed by same-owner success. This is not yield-after-drain and not a pre-join ___LW_REFUSED flag. No sustained 100000 batch was 8 of 8, so the flood was not submitted to gambit-smp. Origin gsi sha256 is still 9eca674b79248987e67d458c9acce7941149f428616caf0aff5defdc93e49d78. The count stays 8/12.
